claims.statement: TVI-CAMS is an internal multi-tenant TESDA compliance working layer for TVI schools running TWSP/CFSP scholarship batches; TESDA's SIS, T2MIS, and BSRS remain the authoritative systems, the tool never holds official standing, and UI copy must never imply official approval or submission.

RLS is the security boundary and UI hiding is usability only — every authorization decision is made by Postgres RLS via app_private.* helper functions (RULES §1.1), and a JS-side tenant filter is a bug even when it returns the right answer because it signals the query was written assuming no RLS (RULES §1.2).

No statement may be executed against the live Supabase project without explicit user permission (RULES §10, [deny] via .claude/settings.json permissions.deny): the rule covers execute_sql including read-only selects, apply_migration, branch create/merge/reset, and edge-function deploys by any route (MCP, CLI, psql), because there is one hosted project and no staging, so an unreviewed statement lands on real tenant data; schema questions are answered from the checked-in migrations and database.types.ts first.

By the 2026-10-24 state recorded first-hand in supabase/migrations/README.md, every migration in its first state table is both recorded and present — including 20260904120000 (repaired and recorded), 20260906120000 (applied transactionally; its ensure_profile_tenant_membership gap is closed) and 20260910120000 (repair-recorded with its full object inventory verified live) — and 20261024071359 (ADR-007) is recorded and applied with its four column assertions verified; 20261024110000 (ADR-008) is the only checked-in migration not applied.

The evidence upload I/O in modules/documents/data/evidence.ts (the private compliance-evidence bucket, signed-URL reads) is written but not exercised: two dashboard toggles (Clerk's Supabase integration and Supabase Third-Party Auth) are still unset under issue #122, so every call fails with an RLS denial indistinguishable from a code defect, and the file must not be debugged against a live project until #122 is closed.

The blocker-gate family (blockingDocuments, blockerCount, blockingDocumentNames) in modules/documents/domain/compliance.ts implements ADR-004 D4 and is unit-tested in tests/unit/doc-blockers.test.ts, but no screen or other code consumes it — it is a ready public domain surface, not live screen behavior.

After any migration (RULES §3 rule 20) the agent must regenerate lib/supabase/database.types.ts and then update the affected mappers and domain types; new migrations are additive with 20260528160300 canonical. The directory is not the ledger: supabase/migrations/README.md is updated in the same PR and a row moves to applied only once the migration has actually run, whereas docs/DATA_MODEL.md stops at seven versions and is history.

Neither the supabase/migrations/ directory listing nor list_migrations alone is authoritative: Supabase keys applied migrations on the version string, so renaming a file makes it look unapplied and hand-run SQL records nothing, and that drift has already happened twice (20260906114735 and 20261024071359 were both renamed to the version Supabase recorded). Objects must be confirmed by name (pg_proc, pg_policies); a policy-set comparison reads as a match no matter what is missing. One policy, public.tenants' "Tenants selectable by Clerk user", is defined by no checked-in migration and omits the is_active check its reviewed counterpart enforces.

The checked schema now extends past the 2026-09-10 record of 18 tables, 36 foreign keys and seven enums: 20260910120000 adds a seven-table billing domain with 16 foreign keys and the billing_type enum, and the newer 20261024071359 (ADR-007) replaces the fixed max_absences count with max_absence_percent on program_billing_rules and tenant_settings and adds attendance_records.excused, so both the dated recorded shape and the checked-in target belong to a record rather than to a fresh read.

The ADR-006 /schools/new write path creates a tenant plus its registered programs atomically: the Server Action composes the validated SchoolCommand (pure rules in modules/tenancy/domain/schoolDraft.ts) and the write goes through modules/tenancy/data/schools.ts's createSchool, which calls the security invoker public.create_school RPC on the Clerk-scoped anon client (never the service-role client), so RLS still evaluates every statement inside the transaction; the screen is gated on the platform-admin axis via the current_user_is_platform_admin() RPC snapshot (getPlatformAdminSnapshot), deliberately not on resolveRouteRole or tenant role, and results distinguish created / duplicate-code / denied (RLS 42501) / sync-failed / unconfigured.

Platform admin is a separate axis from profile_role, not a fifth role value: it is its own public.platform_admins table (RLS enabled with no policies, so it is unreadable and unwritable through the Clerk-scoped anon client and the role cannot be self-granted), resolved in-app only through the security definer public.current_user_is_platform_admin() boolean. Its reach is the school registry only — tenants, qualifications, tenant_qualifications, unassigned profiles, and seating a tenant's first member (whose INSERT policy carries two load-bearing guards: it cannot seat itself, and only into a memberless tenant) — with no policy granting any compliance table (batches, learners, documents, lamr_*, activity_log); granting one is a boundary change that needs its own ADR (RULES §7, ADR-006 P3).

`pnpm test` is `vitest run` (include `tests/unit/**/*.test.ts` in vitest.config.mts) and `tests/unit/` holds 26 spec files at this head, so rule 34's "no test runner yet / placeholder" prose no longer describes the repo. Time-dependent behavior is pinned with vi.setSystemTime rather than the runner clock (batches.test.ts fixes 2026-06-01 for its daysToBilling block); dashboard-domain.test.ts needs no clock because daysToBilling is precomputed on its fixtures.

The post-sign-in open-redirect defense lives in the pure domain function `sanitizeRedirectUrl` (`modules/auth/domain/redirectUrl.ts`), which `app/sign-in/[[...sign-in]]/sign-in-page.tsx` invokes on the attacker-controlled `redirect_url` query param: a trimmed value passes through only if it is a same-origin relative path (single leading slash, no URL scheme, no protocol-relative `//host` form, no backslash tricks); anything else falls back to "/". All post-verification navigations — the `finalize` callbacks and the `startGoogleSignIn` OAuth attempt — target that sanitized value through Clerk's `decorateUrl` rather than a bare URL.

docs/DATA_MODEL.md stops at seven versions and its prose is history rather than current: it still marks 20260906120000 "genuinely missing" (now applied), says /users/new cannot assign anyone until 20260904120000 runs (now applied and recorded), and frames the pending set as behaviour-only — which no longer holds, since ADR-007 and ADR-008 are checked in and unlisted. supabase/migrations/README.md is the ledger that is current, and it dates its own state blocks (2026-10-04, 2026-10-24) rather than standing as a timeless catalog.

Local development is `pnpm install` then `pnpm dev`; `.env.example` documents the Clerk test keys (`pk_test_*`/`sk_test_*`) used by the e2e suite, the Supabase pair is read as `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` + `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` by `lib/supabase/server.ts`, and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is read only by `lib/supabase/service.ts` for the Clerk webhook; when the Supabase pair is unset, `isSupabaseConfigured()` is false and data functions return `unconfigured` snapshots rather than fabricated data.

RULES.md rule 30 fixes the ADR precedence chain one way: ADR-001 supersedes conflicting billing-is-preparation-only PRD/TRD wording, ADR-003 amends ADR-001 §4 (derived packet due_date, P5), ADR-007 supersedes ADR-001's Elig row (20% of total_sessions or 3 consecutive unexcused absences replaces the retired ≥5-absence count), ADR-008 amends ADR-003<|place_holder_mm_span_0442|>P5 for the batch-level deadline only, and ADR-006 supersedes FR-02's "Super Admin is not implemented" while closing platform-admin reach to the school registry — extending it to any compliance table, or letting the operator seat itself into a tenant, needs its own ADR. ADR-002 and ADR-005 stay accepted and load-bearing for scope.

Two schema facts are not wired into any caller: max_absence_percent and attendance_records.excused have no code reference (modules/attendance/domain/eligibility.ts is unbuilt), and modules/batches/data/batches.ts reads `row.billing_deadline ?? null`, so until 20261024110000 is applied every batch reports "not recorded" and no path exists to enter a deadline. Separately, lib/supabase/database.types.ts is out of step in both directions — it lacks the billing tables, `excused` and `max_absence_percent` and still describes `max_absences`, while carrying `billing_deadline` by hand ahead of its migration.

e2e/auth.spec.ts is the single Playwright spec: it obtains a Clerk testing token, visits /dashboard and waits for a redirect to /sign-in, deliberately exercising the requireAuthenticatedUser() gate in app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx rather than proxy.ts; playwright.config.ts boots the app with `pnpm dev` on PORT or :3000 with global.setup.ts as a dependency. No .github/workflows file runs the lint/test/typecheck/e2e loop, so green is a local gate.

The checks that actually bite inside the shared server client are governed by RULES rule 3: lib/supabase/server.ts builds the anon-key client with Clerk's `accessToken` callback (no template, no hand-set Authorization header), and the callback throws the exported NO_CLERK_TOKEN_MESSAGE when Clerk issues no token so the failure surfaces as `sync-failed` instead of an indistinguishable empty `anon` read. tests/unit/supabase-server.test.ts pins both the callback shape and the throw, and is the pattern to copy for other server-boundary code.
